_comment: Vocabulary v0: the reading skills (C2, 2026-09-26; design 2026-09-26-vocabulary.md §1, §4).
A skill is an ability a teacher names. Each one says which demands exercise it
(`opportunity`, ids in demands.json), how a run could show it (`observable`: pitch,
timing, or none, with the parts no run measures under `unobserved`), and the run
conditions for its practice standard and its full one. v0 holds only what the nine
sight-reading rows and the rungs 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 2.2, 2.5, 3.4, 4.5 and 4.6 practise,
plus the two skills the taught-at table needs a coper for (tie, dotted-quarter). A
skill is added when a reader needs it and its observable exists (reviewer decision 2).
Ids are today's concept ids wherever they read as abilities (concepts.json keeps their
display names and finders); `accidentals` is the one new id. `steps`, `skips` and
`eighth-notes` stay concepts but are demands here (interval.step, interval.skip,
rhythm.eighths), and `C-position` is a range v0 measures (range.beyond-position absent):
none is a skill, because a detector finds it.
A rung names a skill in its `requirements` (curriculum.schema.json, since C5): a
ladder state, or reads at a standard. C2's interim table of `mastery.custom` terms and
the build gate's waivers are gone with the terms: each became a predicate or an
`unjudged` requirement the lesson page prints.
The numbers that decide what counts are here, beside the skills (CL11b, L57): the
`support` share every skill reads unless it names its own, and the timing `precision`
of each rhythm skill, with the default the skills whose rhythm is the phrase's fall
back to. They were Part G's pass share and a table in app/src/evidence/evidence.ts;
the values did not change when they moved. A note's name on the screen is supported
practice, never unaided reading (L58): `names-off` stands beside every `guide-off`
of a full standard.
validate.py checks this file against skills.schema.json and its references.

conditions.meaning: The run kept a tempo (Keep tempo), so onsets were timed. Wait has no clock.
conditions.recordedBy: SessionRow.mode and SessionRow.tempoMeasured (T37); a pass with a tempo floor requires it (Scoring.evaluateOutcome)

conditions.meaning: The first reading of this music: not played or heard before this run.
conditions.recordedBy: SessionRow.unseen (C1): true on the first reading of a generated phrase, false when it was heard or read before; absent on anything else, whose first contact no run records. v0's material is the generated phrases.

conditions.meaning: The keys under the score did not mark the next key, so the notes were read and not followed.
conditions.recordedBy: SessionRow.keys.guide (C1): 'off', which the Score screen also writes when the keys are hidden

conditions.meaning: The run played both hands, not one with the other left out or played by the app.
No note's name was on the screen (not the ribbon's label on a marked key, not Wait's line naming the note it waits for), so the notes were read from the staff and not from their names.
conditions.recordedBy: SessionRow.keys.names (C1): false, written with the keys on every run the Score screen records; true where the ribbon labelled a guided key or Wait named the note (Name the note I am waiting for). A row that does not record it is not shown to have had the names off (CL11b, L58).

support.why: A record supports a skill where this share of its counted steps or more was right (C3). It is the share a rung's pass asks of the notes (Part G's default, 90 %), held here as the skills' own since L57, so a change to the rungs' pass no longer re-reads every skill's history. It is applied when evidence is read (the ladder, the transfer policy, the demand readings, the reader), so a change here re-reads every stored record at once. A skill that needs another share names its own `support`; none does.

precision.why: The error a timing skill is about, in quarter-note beats: the smallest distance between where the written rhythm puts a note and where the likely wrong rhythm puts it. A window as wide as this or wider records the wrong rhythm as hits, so at that step timing measures nothing (reviewer decision 6; CL04, L73). This default is the coarsest error any rhythm has, a note moved by an eighth: a skill whose rhythm is the phrase's (every step, or a texture: sight-reading, hand-independence) takes, step by step, the finest precision of the rhythm demands located at the step, and this where none is. A skill with its own `precision` is a rhythm skill, and its demands are the rhythm demands.

skills.sentence: Playing a phrase you have never seen, first time, at a steady tempo: the right notes in the right rhythm.
unobserved: Straight through without stopping: stops and hesitations are not measured (continuity is not built, design §3). That part is reading-ahead.

transfer.why: The right notes and the right rhythm of music never seen: another key signature, another rhythmic surface, the other hand's staff, or both staves at once each change what has to be read at sight.

skills.sentence: Keeping the music going by reading further along the line than the note you are playing.
unobserved: The eyes cannot be seen, and the one sign a run could give of reading ahead (no stop, no hesitation before a new bar) is not measured: continuity is not built (design §3).

skills.sentence: Reading notes on the bass staff by where they sit, not by counting up from a landmark every time.

transfer.why: Notes on the bass staff read by where they sit: another key puts the reading on other lines and spaces, and the bass staff read while the other hand plays is another texture; pitch only, so rhythm is not this skill's.

skills.sentence: Reading notes above and below the staff, on the ledger lines beyond middle C.

transfer.why: Notes beyond the staff: another key uses and alters other ledger notes, and the right hand's ledger lines above the treble staff are other notes than the left hand's below the bass.

skills.sentence: Reading the distance to the next note (a step, a skip, a leap) from its shape on the staff instead of naming every note.
skills.note: Right notes are what a note-namer plays too, in a fixed position (design §2, the generated-exercise trace Q5, when the first finger was printed; since G30 it is not, and the point holds without it). Pitch is the observable; that it shows reading by interval rather than by name rests on the material and the conditions, not on the measurement.

transfer.why: The distance read from its shape: in a fixed C position a note-namer plays the same right notes (the skill's note), so another key or position, the other hand's staff, and both staves at once are what show the shape is read; pitch only, so rhythm is not.

skills.sentence: Moving the hand to a new place when the music leaves the five notes under it.
unobserved: Without a gap in the sound: legato across the shift is not measured.

transfer.why: Moving the hand to a new place: in another key the new places fall on other keys, black ones among them, and the other hand moves the other way; how the hand moves (a thumb passing under, a lift) is measured by no dimension, and another family does not stand in for it.

skills.sentence: Feeling the smaller notes inside the beat, two eighths or four sixteenths to it, and placing them evenly.

precision.why: Two even eighths against the same pair played long-short as a swing, the second note at 2/3 of the beat: 1/6 of a beat apart.

transfer.why: Placing the smaller notes evenly inside the beat: other figures and metres around them, or placing them against the other hand, change it; the key and the hand do not change the timing.

skills.sentence: Holding a note for a beat and a half and placing the eighth after it.

precision.why: The eighth after the dot placed on the beat instead: a displacement of an eighth, half a beat.

transfer.why: A beat and a half and the eighth after it: the same figure in another rhythmic context, or against the other hand, changes it; the key and the hand do not change the timing.

skills.sentence: Holding a note through the tie into the next beat or bar without playing it again.

precision.why: The tie cut short by its written part, the next note early: a displacement of an eighth, half a beat.

skills.note: Timing, for the note after the tie. A tied note played again is an extra key; whether the engine counts it against the run was not checked, so pitch is not claimed.

transfer.why: Holding through the tie into the next beat or bar: another rhythmic context, or the other hand moving over the held note, changes it; the key and the hand do not change the timing.

skills.sentence: Placing a note off the beat, or coming in after a rest on the beat, against a pulse that keeps going.

precision.why: An off-beat note moved onto the beat: a displacement of an eighth, half a beat.

transfer.why: A note off the beat against a pulse that keeps going: another rhythmic context, or the pulse held in the other hand, changes it; the key and the hand do not change the timing.

skills.sentence: Fitting three even notes into the space of two.

precision.why: Triplet eighths at 0, 1/3 and 2/3 of a beat against the rushed sixteenth-sixteenth-eighth at 0, 1/4 and 1/2 (design §4's case): the second note 1/12 of a beat early, the third 1/6.

skills.note: At the rungs' tempi the engine's ±150 ms window cannot tell even triplets from a rushed sixteenth-sixteenth-eighth (design §4; reviewer decision 6). Timing is the observable; the evidence function (C3) refuses it wherever the window is wider than the difference it has to see.

transfer.why: Three even notes in the space of two: another rhythmic context, or twos in the other hand against them, changes it; the key and the hand do not change the timing.

skills.sentence: Feeling two beats of three eighths each, not six equal beats.

precision.why: The compound lilt, a quarter then an eighth (at 0 and 1 in quarters), evened into two dotted eighths (at 0 and 3/4): a quarter of a beat apart.

transfer.why: Two beats of three eighths: other figures inside the compound metre, or the metre held against the other hand, change it; the key and the hand do not change the metre.

skills.sentence: Counting three beats to the bar, and holding a dotted half for all three of them.

precision.why: A dotted half counted as a half, the next note a whole beat early: the bar of three read as a bar of four, or of two.

skills.note: SR2 (the reviewer's ruling on SR1, docs/review/responses/sr1-sightreading-quality.md §1): the copedWithBy of metre.three-four, which 1.4 teaches through its concept 3/4. Added only because the taught-at table needs a coper for it, as tie and dotted-quarter were; no item declares it in targetSkills.

transfer.why: Three beats to the bar: other figures inside the bar of three, or the bar held against the other hand, change it; the key and the hand do not change the metre.

skills.sentence: Remembering the sharps or flats at the start of the line on every note they alter.

transfer.why: Remembering the signature on every note it alters: another signature alters other notes, and the other staff's notes are other notes to alter.

skills.sentence: Reading a sharp, flat or natural written beside a note, and letting it last to the end of the bar.
skills.note: Its concept `accidentals` exists since F2a (3.1 introduces it, 3.3 names it); before that no concept named it — `sharps` and `flats` are the two signs as 3.1 teaches them (notes and key signatures), `chromatic` is moving by semitones (a technique rung). The level-4 row promises an accidental in the bar, which is this.

transfer.why: A sign beside a note, lasting to the bar's end: against another key signature the same sign does another thing (a natural cancelling the signature's sharp), and on the other staff it lands on other notes.

skills.sentence: Reading both staves at once and playing together the notes that sound together.
skills.note: Pitch at the steps where both hands play; the two hands arriving together in time is the full standard's Keep tempo.

transfer.why: Both staves at once: another texture under the melody (a left-hand pattern, a walking bass) and both staves in another key are other reading; the hands are both on every run it can count (its conditions require both), so the hands can never differ for it.

skills.sentence: The hands doing different things at once: a moving left-hand pattern under a melody.

transfer.why: The hands doing different things at once: another left-hand pattern (walking rather than repeating) or another rhythm between the hands changes it; the key does not change the independence.

skills.sentence: Playing the habanera and the tresillo as the left hand's rhythm, and telling the two cells apart on the page and by ear.
unobserved: The cell's identity at tempo: Keep tempo's ±150 ms window cannot separate the habanera from a dotted-pair near-miss at moderate speed, and the evidence refuses timing it cannot resolve (MODE-SHEET.md §2, 'Cannot establish' (ii); ABILITY-MAP.md A7c.1), so no run is evidence that the cell was played as the cell (CD1).
Telling the two cells apart by ear is self-checked (A7c.1's never_credits): no run observes it, and nobody in this process hears music.
skills.note: CD1 (docs/prompts/runs/curriculum-review-2026-10-05/briefs/cells-as-measured-demands.md D4): the copedWithBy of rhythm.habanera and rhythm.tresillo, which makes 'no run is evidence of the cell' a vocabulary fact. Not syncopation (the concept would stop naming rhythm.syncopation) and not subdivision (the 4/4 tresillo's dotted quarters would become subdivision opportunities); not two skills, which would turn concepts into abilities a requirement could name.
